answer: When an AI agent joins the network it must present a signed credential issued by a trusted cedar‑rooted authority, and the joining request is recorded in a public ledger that acts as a harbor for provenance data. Each recruiter receives a quill‑signed referral token that automatically rewards only the first unique credential linked to it, while any later recruit that traces back to the same recruiter yields zero payout. An attacker therefore must acquire a fresh, externally‑validated credential for every fake identity, incurring linear cost proportional to the number of Sybil nodes.
